core_claim: In early March 2020, COVID-19's case map showed where countries were looking — not where the virus was. Tourism flows revealed exactly who was looking the wrong way.

edt_01.label: Hook — A map that already lied
edt_01.title: A map that already lied
edt_01.editorial_notes: 95,124 / 80,271 / 67,332 / 70% must be exact. The hook frames the rest — landing the global picture and the doubt simultaneously.

edt_02.label: The yardstick — Chinese tour groups
edt_02.title: The yardstick: Chinese tour groups
edt_02.editorial_notes: Thailand 1.55m; Japan 1.25m; top 10 = 74% — exact. Explains the proxy.

edt_03.label: The model — OECD-only fit
edt_03.title: The OECD line
edt_03.editorial_notes: Coefficients -8.44 intercept, 1.13 slope, R-squared 0.59 — exact. This is the model that everything else turns on.

edt_04.label: The reveal — under the line
edt_04.title: Below the line
edt_04.editorial_notes: Russia 3 vs 517; Indonesia 2 vs 330; Myanmar 0 vs 110 — exact. Reader should *see* the residual visually before getting numbers — strongly recommend an interactive scatter where the OECD line and the residual gap are clear.

edt_05.label: The other end — Iran, Italy, Korea
edt_05.title: Above the line
edt_05.editorial_notes: Iran 2,922 vs 12; Italy 3,089 vs 156; SK 5,621 vs 392 — exact. The 'other end' completes the model's two diagnoses.

edt_06.label: The asymmetry — OECD vs not
edt_06.title: A surveillance gap, by group
edt_06.editorial_notes: -0.85 log-units; 43% of OECD-predicted level; 64% vs 56% — exact. Group-level number for those who want the systematic claim.

edt_07.label: The multiplier
edt_07.title: What the model says is missing
edt_07.editorial_notes: Russia 172x, Indonesia 165x, Myanmar 110x — exact. Subsequent peer-reviewed multipliers (Iran 34x, Italy 73x, Spain 161x) come from det_04. Frame as 'the model implies', not 'we proved'.

edt_08.label: Close — Reading the gaps
edt_08.title: Reading the gaps
edt_08.editorial_notes: Pure narrative close. No new data — synthesis of the framing. End on the move itself ('fit on the part of the world that measures well, read the gap').
